title: Booking Ray Charles
summary: Stovall booked Ray Charles from $350 a night to $5,000, never made money, and recalls Rip Robert playing in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He used to call his guitar that, he used to call his guitar the Devil. Yeah, yeah. What do you know about Ray Charles?

Well, Ray was a good friend of mine, was a good friend of mine. I knew when he started out, I remember when he used to travel, he came in his band and arrived in a little, at that time they used to make a little car called a disorder stage with a rag on the top, because all the band was buying him, you know. He had a little stuff placed in their back. And Ray used to come to Pensacola, I used to come to Pensacola, we used to play around Alabama and Pensacola pretty often. So Ray would come in there, and I met him one day, and we got to be friends. But, and I booked Ray, I used to pay Ray $350 a night, $400 a night. I used to book him off and off. We used to book him off and off. We used to work in New York together. We used to travel with a boy named D. Clark then. And we was in the same hotel together. So I booked him. And last time I booked him, he was $5,000. I lost money on him. I have never made money. I didn't make money when I paid him for $350 a night. I couldn't make money on him. I played him all around New York and couldn't draw a card away. I came to Pensacola at the Auditore. When he was $5,000, I lost money on him. So I told him that night, I said, I don't know you or no me, so we left it off. But I never could make money with him.
New Orleans, you mean he just worked in?

Well I never played in here. I had a guy named Rip Robert always played in here. Rip was his buddy, you know. I would play New Orleans. But after he got big, when he was small I played him all around Kenner, I played him on the River in Lincoln High School, I played him all around.

Yeah, right, and had the goods with him too, you see. So then after he got real big, big, then he started doing good for the Rip Robert, you see. So I played him out of town, Pensacola, I couldn't make that money with him. But he was a good friend of mine in Lincoln High School.
Well, I think he was good friends with your country, wasn't he?
Well they knew each other, yeah I think so. I think Slim met him in Pensacola at the same time I met him. Because Slim was with us then out there, you know. So I don't know how to do that.
